inline:The target's 'only if' condition is empirically refuted by the record's own distribution: every ordinarily-guarded module lost 4/4 to 6/7 mutations under the same installation, so the planted-failure gate neither reliably constrains nor even reliably detects, and the target never reconciles its necessity claim with the base-rate failure of the same ritual elsewhere.
The problem demands an account of the 3-of-26 distribution. The target treats compile.py's 1/9 as the informative cell ('partial constraint') while ignoring that 22-26 of 26 mutations were lost in modules subjected to the same shown-to-fail-first installation. If planted-failure installation were necessary and sufficient for constraint, those modules would constrain; they lost mutations at far higher rates than compile.py. The target's mechanism ('ritual gate ... expectation built into acceptance criteria') applies equally to all 26 modules, so it cannot explain why compile.py uniquely retained 8/9 mutations — the actually anomalous datum is inverted in the target's account, which reads the low-loss module as the explained case and the high-loss majority as background.
